body: Academic and quant evidence explains *why* the legends' ideas work. Novy-Marx found **gross profitability predicts returns about as well as book-to-market**, and the two are negatively correlated, so combining them is powerful ([Novy-Marx](https://www.ivey.uwo.ca/media/3775548/novy-marx.pdf)). AQR's **Quality Minus Junk** earns significant returns across 24 countries ([NBER](https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f69835.pdf)). **Value and momentum** premia appear across eight markets and asset classes ([AQR](https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Research/Journal-Article/Value-and-Momentum-Everywhere)). The small-cap premium reappears only **once junk is excluded** ([Asness et al.](https://research-api.cbs.dk/ws/files/57307999/lasse_heje_pedersen_et_al_size_matters_if_you_control_your_junk_publishersversion.pdf)). That directly supports the "S" in SQGLP and the "Small" in SMILE, but only with a quality filter attached. "Buffett's Alpha" found Berkshire's alpha **becomes insignificant after controlling for low-beta and quality factors**, with average leverage of about 1.7:1. In the authors' words, it is "a reward for leveraging cheap, safe, quality stocks" ([NBER w19681](https://www.nber.org/papers/w19681.pdf)). Renaissance's Medallion fund, at about 66% gross and 39% net a year from 1988 to 2018, is the exception that proves the limits. It is closed to outsiders, built on leverage and execution infrastructure, and RenTec's own external funds are "relatively mundane" ([Institutional Investor](https://www.institutionalinvestor.com/article/b1k2fymby99nj0/Famed-Medallion-Fund-Stretches-Explanation-to-the-Limit-Professor-Claims)). Retail investors can harvest slow factors such as quality, value and momentum. They cannot compete in high-frequency trading.

`theme:sector-auto-oems` · confidence: single-source · tickers: MARUTI, M&M, TATAMOTORS, BAJAJ-AUTO, HEROMOTOCO, TVSMOTOR, EICHERMOT, ASHOKLEY

**How it makes money:** Design, assemble and distribute vehicles; margin = mix x pricing - commodities, high operating leverage.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Retail (Vahan/FADA) vs wholesale (SIAM) growth
- Market share by segment
- EBITDA margin
- Realisation/vehicle & mix (SUV, premium 2W)
- Dealer inventory days
- Exports share
- EV penetration & PLI eligibility

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Commodities -> component suppliers (~60–70% of cost) -> OEM (design, brand, assembly) -> dealers (thin margins) -> financiers. OEMs with brand pricing power capture most of the profit; dealers and many suppliers are squeezed.

**Cycle drivers:** Rates & financing, rural income/monsoon, fuel prices, regulatory cost-push, GST, infra/freight for CVs, product cycles.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- Vahan dashboard (daily registrations)
- FADA monthly retail + inventory days
- SIAM monthly wholesales
- Tractor sales (TMA)
- PPAC diesel consumption
- GSTN e-way bills
- Auto loan growth (RBI sectoral deployment)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: right product cycle (SUVs, premium bikes, scooters), share gains, pricing power. Losers: missed segment shifts, EV capex without demand, overseas acquisitions (JLR debt for Tata Motors 2018–20).

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 18–30x; 2W leaders up to 35x in upcycles. CVs: buy at peak P/E on trough earnings (FY21), sell at low P/E on peak earnings. Auto sector ~24x vs 23x LTA (Oct 2026).

**Current state (Nov 2026):** SIAM Oct 2026: PV 5,19,060 (+12.4%), 2W 25,77,810 (+16.1%) wholesale. FADA Oct 2026 retail: PV 5,07,768 (−14.2%), 2W 23.2 lakh (−28.4%) on Diwali shifting to November and a high GST-cut base (Oct 2025).

**Classic traps:**
- Wholesale channel-stuffing ahead of festivals
- A GST-cut demand pull-forward read as a trend
- EV-transition winners priced before profits
- Cyclical CVs valued on peak earnings

body: **Summary:** Indian defence companies sell to effectively one customer, the Ministry of Defence, under long-cycle contracts. Profit comes from execution of an order backlog (HAL aircraft and helicopters, BEL radars and electronics, BDL missiles, shipyards), plus spares, MRO and growing exports. Margins are cost-plus or negotiated, and indigenisation content is rising. Private players such as Solar (explosives), Data Patterns and Astra grow on niche technology and exports. Key metrics: order book/revenue (HAL ~8x, BEL ~3x), order inflow against guidance, execution (revenue growth), EBITDA margin, advances from customers (strong cash), working capital, export share and indigenisation %. Cycle drivers: the defence capital budget (~₹1.8–2.2 lakh cr capital outlay), DAC Acceptance of Necessity approvals, then Cabinet Committee on Security sanction, then contract signing, plus positive indigenisation lists, geopolitical events (Operation Sindoor, May 2025) and supply-chain bottlenecks (GE F404 engines for Tejas). Lead indicators: DAC AoN announcements (PIB), the Union Budget capital outlay, CCS approvals, MoD contract signing releases, SIPRI data, defence export figures. Winners (BEL, HAL over 2020–25) had a monopoly position, nominated orders, technology transfer and a cash-rich balance sheet. Losers among pre-2014 private entrants (Reliance Naval, ABG Shipyard) took big contracts with weak execution and debt. Valuation: historical P/E 14–21x; re-rated to 30–60x+ by 2024–25 (HAL 28x against 14x historical; BEL 41x against 21x). Nov 2026: DAC approvals in FY27 total ₹1.62 lakh cr. BEL Q1 FY27 inflows were weak (book-to-bill below 1). As of Sep 2026, HAL traded at ~32x FY27e and BEL at ~42x. Traps: DAC approvals are not orders, and multiples priced for perfection. Sources: [1](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/hindustan-aeronautics-bharat-electronics-and-bdl-q2-revenue-rises-across-defence-ps-us-but-profit-growth-varies/article-203496/) · [2](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/bel-hal-bdl-shares-targets-for-defence-stocks-after-rs-1-1-lakh-crore-dac-approvals-553813-2026-09-08) · [3](https://www.angelone.in/news/stocks/hal-and-bel-understanding-order-books-execution-and-revenue) Links: about `case_study:defence-psu-rerating`
